```{julia}
#| tags: [parameters]
#| output: false
# Defaults for running the cells outside Quarto. Under `quarto render` the front-matter
# `params` (overridden by `-P name:value` or `--execute-params file.yml`, see
# render_bb_reports.sh) are already defined as constants, so these assignments are skipped.
@isdefined(cma) || (cma = Dict("r" => 0.005, "rb_real" => 0.015, "re_real" => 0.045))
@isdefined(period) || (period = [1935, 2025])   # historical sample bootstrapped
@isdefined(block_size) || (block_size = 5)      # (mean) block length in years
@isdefined(random_block) || (random_block = true)  # stationary bootstrap
@isdefined(T) || (T = 100)                      # simulated years
@isdefined(horizons) || (horizons = [1, 5, 10, 20, 30, 50, 100])  # horizon table years, ≤ T
@isdefined(n_scen) || (n_scen = 10000)
@isdefined(seed) || (seed = 1234)
```

```{julia}
#| output: false
import Pkg
Pkg.activate(joinpath(@__DIR__, "..", ".."); io = devnull)

using MacroFinanceScenarios
using MacroFinanceScenarios.IbbotsonSinquefield
using MacroFinanceScenarios.EDA
using MacroFinanceScenarios.ScenariosEvaluation
using CSV, DataFrames, Random, Statistics, TimeSeries
using Plots

show_table(t; title = "", digits = 2) =
    display(HTML(sprint(io -> print_table(io, t; backend = :html, digits, title))))

# Everything loaded and computed is in decimal log units; the report shows percent. Means,
# std and percentiles scale by 100; skewness, kurtosis, autocorrelations and correlations
# do not, and `neg` (share of negative values) is already in percent.
pct(sc::Scenarios) = Scenarios(100 .* sc.data, sc.names, sc.start_year)
function pct(df::DataFrame; cols)
    out = copy(df)
    for c in cols
        out[!, c] = 100 .* out[!, c]
    end
    return out
end
moment_cols = [:mean, :std, :min, :p25, :p50, :p75, :max]   # describe_series columns in %
span(p) = "$(p[1])–$(p[2])"

vars = [:r, :rb_real, :re_real]
# Quarto passes the `cma` mapping as a Dict{String}; match_means takes a NamedTuple and
# rejects unknown names.
targets = (; (Symbol(k) => Float64(v) for (k, v) in cma)...)
```

## Data and assumptions

Annual real returns from `data/shiller_annual.csv` (written by `export_shiller_annual.jl`):
the real T-bill return `r`, the real bond return `rb_real` and the real equity return
`re_real`, `{julia} span(period)`. Each variable is shifted by a constant so that its sample
mean equals the capital market assumption (CMA); std, skewness, autocorrelation and
correlations are unchanged. The CMA are means of annual **log** returns: a simple expected
return `E[R]` corresponds to roughly `log(1 + E[R]) − σ²/2`.

```{julia}
raw = TimeArray(CSV.File(joinpath(@__DIR__, "..", "..", "data", "shiller_annual.csv"));
                timestamp = :timestamp)
data = subperiod(raw[vars...], (period[1], period[2]))
hist = match_means(data, targets)

show_table(DataFrame(variable = String.(vars),
                     historical_mean = [100mean(values(data[v])) for v in vars],
                     cma_target = [100get(targets, v, mean(values(data[v]))) for v in vars],
                     shift = [100(mean(values(hist[v])) - mean(values(data[v]))) for v in vars]);
           title = "Means of annual log real returns (%)")
show_table(DataFrame(parameter = ["sample", "years", "block size", "block lengths",
                                  "simulated years", "scenarios", "seed"],
                     value = [span(period), string(length(hist)), string(block_size),
                              random_block ? "random (stationary bootstrap)" : "fixed",
                              string(T), string(n_scen), string(seed)]);
           title = "Parameters")
```

Units: returns and moments below are annual log values in percent, except where a table or
chart says *simple rate* (`exp(·) − 1` of the log rate, in percent) or *wealth* (of 1
invested); skewness, excess kurtosis, autocorrelations and correlations are unit-free.

## Historical moments

The matched sample that is bootstrapped (means = CMA targets).

```{julia}
hist_moments = describe_series(hist)
hist_cor = correlation_table(hist)
hist_pct = pct(hist_moments; cols = moment_cols)
show_table(hist_pct; title = "Matched sample, $(span(period))")
show_table(hist_cor; title = "Correlations, $(span(period))")
```

## Simulation

Each simulated year is one whole historical year (so its cross-sectional correlation is
kept), drawn in blocks of consecutive years (keeping autocorrelation up to the block
length). Blocks are circular — they wrap from the last year to the first — so every year
is drawn with the same probability and the simulated mean equals the CMA target in
expectation. No moment matching is applied after the simulation: the gap between the
achieved mean and the target is bootstrap noise, summarised by its standard error (std of
the per-path means / √n_scen).

```{julia}
sc = block_bootstrap(hist, T, n_scen; block_size, random_block, rng = MersenneTwister(seed))
path_means = dropdims(mean(sc.data; dims = 2); dims = 2)   # n_vars × n_scen
achieved = DataFrame(variable = String.(sc.names),
                     target = [100mean(values(hist[v])) for v in sc.names],
                     simulated = 100vec(mean(path_means; dims = 2)),
                     se = 100vec(std(path_means; dims = 2)) ./ sqrt(n_scen))
achieved.z = (achieved.simulated .- achieved.target) ./ achieved.se
show_table(achieved; title = "Mean over all years and paths vs. target (%)")
println("Simulated years $(first(scenario_years(sc)))–$(last(scenario_years(sc))).")
```

## Fan charts

5–95 and 25–75 percentile bands, median, and the CMA target (dashed).

```{julia}
μ_target = Dict(v => mean(values(hist[v])) for v in vars)
fans(vars; kwargs...) = [fan(sc, v; μ = μ_target[v], μ_label = "CMA target", kwargs...) for v in vars]
```

### Cumulative wealth

```{julia}
#| fig-cap: "Wealth of 1 invested, real"
plot(fans(vars; kind = :wealth)...; layout = (1, 3), size = (1000, 330), ylabel = "wealth")
```

### Annualised returns

Geometric-average annual return over the first `h` years, `exp(sum(x_1..h)/h) − 1`.

```{julia}
#| fig-cap: "Annualised simple real rates"
plot(fans(vars; kind = :annualised, simple = true, scale = 100)...;
     layout = (1, 3), size = (1000, 330), ylabel = "%")
```

## Evaluation

### Per-path moments

Statistics computed within each simulated path, then summarised across scenarios; the
`historical` column is the matched sample. `neg` is the percent of years with a negative
value. Autocorrelation beyond a block is lost, so with a small `block_size` the within-path
`ar1` is biased towards 0 relative to history.

```{julia}
for (name, t) in path_moments(pct(sc); hist = hist_pct)
    show_table(t; title = String(name))
end
```

### Correlations

Correlations computed within each simulated path, then summarised across scenarios. The
matrix is the mean across paths. In the pair table, `historical` is the correlation in the
sample and `hist_rank` the share of paths with a correlation at or below it. Each path
covers `{julia} T` years and the sample `{julia} length(hist)`, so the bands show what a
`{julia} T`-year window looks like, not a test of the historical correlation.

```{julia}
show_table(mean_path_correlations(sc); title = "Mean within-path correlations")
show_table(path_correlations(sc; hist = hist_cor); title = "Pairs")
```

### Horizon percentiles

Annualised returns: the geometric-average annual return over `h` years,
`exp(sum(x_1..h)/h) − 1`, in percent.

```{julia}
function horizon_tables(vars; kind, label)
    for v in vars
        t = select(horizon_percentiles(sc; vars = [v], horizons = filter(<=(T), horizons), kind,
                                       probs = [0.0, 0.05, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.95, 1.0],
                                       simple = true), Not(:variable))
        t = DataFrames.rename(t, :p0 => :min, :p100 => :max)
        t = pct(t; cols = names(t, Not([:horizon, :year])))
        show_table(t; title = "$v, $label")
    end
end
horizon_tables(vars; kind = :annualised, label = "annualised (simple rate, %)")
```

### Drawdowns

Maximum drawdown of wealth (in %) and the longest spell below a previous peak (in years),
per path over the first `horizon` simulated years (50 by default, at most `T`).

```{julia}
function dd_table(s; horizon = 50)
    horizon <= size(s.data, 2) || throw(ArgumentError("horizon $horizon exceeds the $(size(s.data, 2)) simulated years"))
    t = drawdown_table(Scenarios(s.data[:, 1:horizon, :], s.names, s.start_year))
    rows = t.statistic .== "max_drawdown"
    num = names(t, Not([:variable, :statistic]))
    t[rows, num] .*= 100
    return t
end
dd_h = min(50, T)
show_table(dd_table(sc; horizon = dd_h); title = "Real, first $dd_h years")
```
